With shipments of GPUs and other gear repeatedly going missing, new reports suggest thieves are becoming increasingly ambitious and sophisticated as the heists become more lucrative. According to the Bay Area News Group, police suspect that sophisticated thieves stole $11.4 million worth of Nvidia equipment that was supposed to ship from Oakland to Fort Worth, Texas. A vehicle containing six pallets was picked up in Oakland on August 29 as planned, but no one realized the shipment was missing until early September. The theft follows several over the past year involving Nvidia and other companies involved in the AI data center buildout.

latest.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China - The Verge
latest.summary: The government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies. Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their du...
highlights: The government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies. Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company’s H200 AI chips. According to The New York Times, New Matrix is on the list of approved firms, yet its offices are empty, “a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be.” In fact, the paper could find little evidence that the company exists in any meaningful way:. What little information can be found about New Matrix is concerning. Its owners have ties to a Chinese private equity firm that has been blacklisted by the US government since 2024. And according to the Times, this is not a rare lapse in oversight, but a troubling pattern of companies connected to entities with national-security-related trade restrictions being approved to purchase Nvidia chips.

latest.title: US approved Nvidia chip sales to China-linked firms - The Jerusalem Post
latest.summary: # Trump's Nvidia chip deal with China raises security concerns over approved buyers - report. ## A New York Times investigation found that Chinese firms cleared to handle Nvidia AI chips have ties to ...
highlights: # Trump's Nvidia chip deal with China raises security concerns over approved buyers - report. ## A New York Times investigation found that Chinese firms cleared to handle Nvidia AI chips have ties to blacklisted entities and military contractors. The Trump administration approved Chinese companies with ties to US-blacklisted entities and military contractors to purchase or handle advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips, raising questions about the effectiveness of Washington's national security screening process, *The New York Times* reported in an investigation detailed on Saturday. Among the companies approved by the US Commerce Department was New Matrix, a Chinese firm established just 17 months ago whose registered office in an industrial park outside Beijing appeared vacant when visited by *Times* reporters. The findings are part of a broader pattern identified by the newspaper in which Chinese companies approved to handle Nvidia's H200 processors maintain corporate links to entities subject to US national security restrictions.

According to the New York Times, China's secret service reportedly recruited Alice Huang of Megaspeed to spy on the Nvidia CEO. Here is what we know and what we don't. The New York Times reports that Alice Huang, an executive at data center company Megaspeed, was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. The target was Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia. Three US House committees have summoned him to a closed-door hearing on November 18. The case concerns AI chips and who is allowed to buy them. **MSS** is the Ministry of State Security, China's main intelligence agency, described by Engadget as the equivalent of the CIA. **Megaspeed** is a data center company based in Singapore and a customer of Nvidia. **Export controls** are US bans on selling the most advanced AI chips to China. The Engadget account, which relays the New York Times, says the MSS allegedly recruited Alice Huang to gather information on American AI plans.
